issues.legal_issue: Statutory redetermination of land-acquisition compensation is available on the basis of an award by the reference court, not an appellate judgment.
material_facts: The applicant sought redetermination of compensation under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, relying on a High Court judgment in an appeal under Section 54.
The judgment relied on was an appellate judgment, not an award by the reference court.
issues.conclusion: The applicant was not entitled to redetermination based on the High Court’s appellate judgment; any entitlement under Section 28A could be based only on an award of the reference court.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28A(1) permits redetermination by reference to an award of the court under Part III of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. The court means the principal civil court of original jurisdiction under Section 3(d); an appellate court deciding an appeal under Section 54, which falls under Part VIII, is outside Section 28A. The Court relied on Jose Antonio Cruz Dos R. Rodriguese v. Land Acquisition Collector (1996) 6 SCC 746 and Bharatsing v. State of Maharashtra (2017) SCC OnLine SC 1453.

predicates.land_acquisition_redetermination_claim: A person seeks statutory redetermination of compensation arising from a land acquisition.
predicates.claim_based_on_appellate_judgment: The person bases the requested redetermination on a judgment delivered by an appellate court rather than an award by the reference court.

issues.definition: When a person seeks statutory redetermination of land-acquisition compensation based on an appellate judgment, that redetermination is unavailable on that basis.
